liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- Jerry's introduction of Viola Lee suggests he was tripping heavily [3]
- Young Jerry's vocals are gentle, and the introduction is funny [4]
- Vocal harmonies are very tight and sound inspired by the Beach Boys [4]
- Sweet early version sung with the band's best early attempts at harmony [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd66-07-03 t01 Dancin' In The Street**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd66-07-03 t02 I Know You Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd66-07-03 t03 He Was A Friend Of Mine**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd66-07-03 t04 Next Time You See Me**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd66-07-03 t05 Viola Lee Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd66-07-03 t06 Big Boss Man**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd66-07-03 t07 Sittin' On Top Of The World**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd66-07-03 t08 Don't Ease Me In**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-07-03.139751.sbd.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 9 songs; 37 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape cuts: a significant portion of I Know You Rider and of Sittin' On Top Of The World is missing [1]
- **gd66-07-03.sbd.unknown.40.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 32 min; rated 3.8/5 by 20 [2]. Said about its sound: Listener Daniel Kessler reports several digispots in the recording; Soundboard with really nice sound quality; Recording cuts in quickly at the start, but the voices are clear and sound great [2][3][6]

## Around the show

- Per liner notes, the Dead played two sets, with the group Love playing between them [1]
- Fits on one CD with the 3-25-66 show, with only Next Time You See Me repeated [3]
- The song later became an extended piece, as in the psychedelic Sept. 16th, '66 version on Vintage Dead [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-07-03.139751.sbd.miller.clugston.flac1648**: transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Master Soundboard 10" Reel @15ips 1/2trk > Dat (16/48); Transfer Info: Sony PCM-R500 (16/48) > Tascam DA-3000 > Adobe Audition >… [1]. Also: Source is a DAT at 16/48 from Charlie Miller, who also did the transfer; circulating copies are 16/44 [1]
- **gd66-07-03.sbd.unknown.40.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by See Notes; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Went to abgd, later to etree [2]
